dataset_family: Shanghai Memory Study (Huashan Hospital memory clinic, Fudan University; 116 MCI: 41 converters / 75 non-converters) for the arm that supports; ADNI (102 MCI: 25/77) for the arm that does not
method_family: SVM (linear or non-linear kernel, chosen by balanced accuracy) on concatenated sMRI (FreeSurfer thickness/volume) and static/dynamic rs-fMRI (ALFF/dALFF, ICA FC/dFC) features pre-selected by group difference, plus clinical variables (age, sex, education, MMSE, APOE4); feature-level fusion, stratified 10-fold CV in each cohort
same_sample_or_cohort_as: P-532 (possible shared recruitment site: Huashan Hospital, Fudan University; participant overlap not verified)
what_it_shows: The study tests adding clinical variables (age, sex, education, MMSE, APOE4) to the combined MRI model (sMRI+fMRI) for 3-year MCI-to-AD conversion in two cohorts. In SMS, MRI+clinical reached AUC 0.93 / ACC 88.7%, against 0.91 / 82.7% for MRI alone, 0.90 for fMRI alone, 0.81 for sMRI alone and 0.85 for clinical-only. In ADNI, MRI+clinical reached AUC 0.86 / ACC 79.0%, against 0.86 / 81.6% for MRI alone. The authors call the ADNI result 'unimproved ... with even lower sensitivity'.
why: PDF identity: the title, authors (Chen Z., Chen K., Li Y., ..., Zhao Q., Yang L.; Huashan Hospital, Fudan University), Hum Brain Mapp 2024 45:e26529 and the DOI match the P-554 block. The comparison relevant to VF-15 is MRI (sMRI+fMRI) versus MRI+clinical. Adding fMRI to sMRI is fusion of a second imaging modality, not auxiliary information. That comparison was run in both cohorts and the results diverge. In SMS it fits both wordings: adding clinical information including MMSE to the imaging model improved it (AUC 0.91 to 0.93, ACC 82.7 to 88.7), and the fused model beat every single-source model, although the margin over fMRI alone is small (0.93 vs 0.90). In ADNI it fits neither: AUC was unchanged at 0.86 and accuracy fell (81.6 to 79.0). Because the same study's second cohort does not reproduce the gain, 'partly' on both wordings, with the SMS arm named as the part shown. Further caveats: (1) The imaging features were selected by t-tests on the whole SMS cohort before cross-validation (p.6), so the SMS internal estimates, on which the supporting result rests, are optimistically biased. (2) The ADNI 'external validation' re-trains and cross-validates within ADNI using the SMS-selected features ('the models constructed from SMS cohort were tuned when validated on ADNI cohort', p.12). It is therefore a second internal CV, not an external test of the fitted model. (3) There are no significance tests; the samples are small (41 and 25 converters); and the fusion is plain SVM concatenation, not an auxiliary-data-aware architecture. (4) The clinical gain in SMS coincides with SMS converters having lower MMSE and more APOE4 carriers, differences absent in ADNI (Table 1, p.7). The authors attribute the divergence to this cohort difference. Independence: the SMS arm is a non-ADNI dataset family (Chinese memory-clinic cohort), which would be new for VF-15, whose three supporters are all ADNI. The ADNI arm shares its dataset family with P-3, P-104 and P-81. Possible shared recruitment site with P-532, whose external cohort is 22 MCI from Huashan Hospital (registry row); I did not verify participant overlap. No shared authors with the supporters (Luo et al.; Shen, Zhu et al.; Cao, Ma, Nayak, Duong). Peer-reviewed journal article, not a preprint.

quotes.quote: Besides, when the MRI features were combined with clinical parameters, the mixed imaging-clinical model (MRI + clinical) performed slightly better than the integrated imaging model (MRI, i.e., sMRI + fMRI) as indicated by all indices.

Consequently, the imaging-clinical model obtained an improved prediction capability than imaging model on SMS, supporting the contribution of clinical features, but unimproved results on ADNI with even lower sensitivity.

Besides, the prediction models using only clinical information (age, gender, years of education, MMSE score, APOE E4 status) and their combination with MRI features, were also constructed using SVM and evaluated.
Finally, the features showing significant difference between MCI_C and MCI_NC patients were selected as the inputs of following prediction models.
Specifically, the models constructed from SMS cohort were tuned when validated on ADNI cohort, using same selected MRI predictors as inputs.
Totally, 41 MCI_C (average age 72 ± 6.7 years; 16 male) and 75 MCI_NC (average age 69 ± 7.8 years; 37 male) were included in this study.
Accordingly, 25 MCI_C and 77 MCI_NC in ADNI dataset with sMRI and fMRI at baseline were included in this study.
